_fixture_note: A saved DOM capture as produced by CAPTURE_SOURCE in scripts/perplexity.mjs, used to test
parseAnswerCapture() without a network, a browser or an X display.
PROVENANCE, stated plainly: this is HAND-AUTHORED against the capture shape that
CAPTURE_SOURCE emits, not a recording of a live Perplexity answer page. It could not be a
recording — as of 2026-08-05 nobody has logged into the automation browser, so every real
run stops at the login wall (that is the R702 acceptance evidence). It is therefore a
CONTRACT fixture: it pins the parser's behaviour on the shapes the parser must survive, and
each entry below exists to exercise one specific rule.
RE-CUT IT FROM A REAL PAGE the moment a session exists, in one command:
scripts/perplexity.mjs ask "who won the 2026 Tour de France" --dump-capture \
then delete this note and re-run pnpm test. If the tests still pass, the parser survived the
real markup; if they do not, the failure is the point of the fixture.
title: What changed in Node 22 | Perplexity

answer.text: Node.js 22 ships the require(esm) interop behind a flag, promotes the WebSocket client to stable, and enables V8 12.4 with the Maglev compiler on supported architectures [1]. The default V8 heap limit now scales with available memory rather than sitting at a fixed 4 GB [2]. It became the Active LTS line in October 2024 [3].
